reviews.one_line_contribution: It claims the raw-vs-distilled memory disagreement is not about abstraction level at all but about two nameable content classes inside items — source-scene object-to-receptacle bindings (valuable only when the deployment scene overlaps the training scene, harmful otherwise) and failure-to-repair pairs (scene-invariant) — and it tests this causally by transplanting each cue into and out of six representations at matched injected-token budgets, predicting that representation identity has no residual effect once the two cue indicators are conditioned on.
reviews.closest_prior_work: SkillEvolBench, arXiv:2605.24117 (verified via the literature command; its indexed abstract reads 'raw trajectory reuse often outperforming distilled skills due to discarded contextual cues'). This is the sharpest threat precisely because the proposal is its direct sequel: the causal story — distillation discards contextual cues, and that is why raw wins — is already asserted in the prior work's own abstract. The delta here is naming two specific cue classes, transplanting them, and splitting by scene overlap, which SkillEvolBench does not do (no token-matched comparison, no seen/unseen split, no cue identification). That is a real but bounded advance: the headline framing is inherited, and what is new is one notch of mechanism. Two further papers erode the framing. arXiv:2608.15008 'Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents' (verified) already reports a controlled harness over text records, structural stores, hierarchical stores and refinement-based memories finding regime-dependent trade-offs and that no substrate dominates — i.e. 'the abstraction/substrate is not the operative variable' is partly published, though without cue-level attribution or transplants. The proposal cites this ID in Related Work as 'substrate routing' but never confronts it as a competitor for its central framing. arXiv:2603.02473 'Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory' (found in my search, not verified with the paper command) reports raw chunk storage matching or exceeding fact extraction and summarization, and attributes variance to the retrieval method rather than the write representation — an independent partial pre-emption of P5's null. SEC itself I verified as a real non-arXiv paper: Semantic Scholar indexes 'Experience Retrieval Compression for Continual Adaptation of LLM Agents' (AIEA 2026, 2 citations) with the four-field unit of task type, key decisions, failure reason and repair action exactly as described.
reviews.strongest_objection: The two named cues are not orthogonal to a simpler explanation the design cannot rule out: procedure copying from a near-duplicate demonstration. On ALFWorld, 'seen scene, different task instance' tasks in the same room share object types, receptacle inventory and admissible-action phrasing, so a retrieved same-room raw trajectory is close to a step-by-step solution the agent can imitate. Raw's seen-scene advantage may therefore be action-sequence copyability, not the binding fact. The load-bearing ablation makes this worse rather than better: minus-B replaces receptacle identities with placeholders, which simultaneously (a) removes the binding content, (b) destroys the copyable action sequence, since the actions are 'go to fridge / open fridge', and (c) degrades the item's surface fluency and parsability. So a confirmed P2 is equally consistent with the binding hypothesis, the procedure-copying hypothesis, and plain text corruption, and the decoy control only isolates token load, not any of these. The proposal half-knows this — action ordering is pre-registered as a third cue — but only as a contingency triggered by a residual in P5, i.e. it is tested only if the main claim has already failed, which is backwards for a competing explanation of the primary result. A related but secondary version of the same problem: all distilled forms are written by the 27B while the pool and the primary evaluation are on the 120B, so the raw-vs-distilled gap magnitude is partly a writer-capability artifact (the transplant arms mitigate this for the mechanism claim but not for P1's effect size). Second-order but real: P3 assumes foreign bindings are wrong, yet AI2-THOR receptacle semantics are stereotyped across rooms (food in fridges, utensils in drawers), so a foreign binding is often approximately correct; a null on P3 would then be read as 'bindings do not matter' when the true reading is 'the manipulation was weak'.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Promote the procedure-copying cue to a third arm of the main factorial rather than a fallback: add minus-P (permute or paraphrase the action sequence while keeping receptacle names intact) crossed with minus-B, so binding content and copyable procedure are separated in the confirmatory run rather than after it. 2) Implement minus-B as a consistent re-labeling with valid-but-wrong receptacle names drawn from the same vocabulary, not as placeholders, so surface form, fluency and token count are preserved and only the referent changes. 3) Add the missing scene-agnostic prior control (see missing_baseline). 4) Replace P5's 'residual within MDE' with a pre-registered equivalence test (TOST) whose bound is tied to the effect being explained — e.g. 30 percent of the measured raw-vs-insight seen-scene gap — because a 4-point residual declared 'within a 5-point MDE' would be the same order as SEC's published +7.7 and would not support 'abstraction per se is inert'; and report attenuation-corrected cue coefficients using the error rate from the 200-item annotator audit, since noisy binary cue indicators under-adjust and inflate the residual the proposal wants to show is zero. 5) State up front that ALFWorld already ships valid-seen and valid-unseen splits and give per-split n; the risk section's framing ('a room-level split may need to be by room type') reads as though this were an open problem and invites doubt about whether the primary contrast is even constructible. 6) Run at least one distilled arm with the 120B as writer to bound the writer-capability confound. 7) Given the budget, drop the WebShop analogue (admittedly loose) and the R4/R6 arms before dropping seeds.
reviews.missing_baseline: A scene-agnostic aggregate binding prior: a 60-token receptacle prior mined over ALL training scenes ('apples are usually in the fridge, knives in the drawer') rather than from the source scene, injected in the same slot and at the same token count as the plus-B table. Without it, a confirmed P2 cannot distinguish 'the agent needs THIS scene's bindings' from 'the agent needs ANY receptacle prior and the source-scene table happens to be a correct instance of one' — and the foreign-binding arm does not cover this, since foreign bindings are specific-and-wrong whereas an aggregate prior is general-and-mostly-right. This control is also what makes the paper's practical claim land or collapse: if a scene-agnostic 60-token prior recovers most of raw's seen-scene advantage, the whole seen/unseen framing is deflated into 'ALFWorld agents lack a commonsense receptacle prior'. A cheaper second omission: a bindings-only memory (the 60-token table with no trajectory, insight or record around it) as the token-efficiency upper bound; the instruction-slot arm approximates this but confounds slot with content.

Judgement of the proposal's own check: it is well above the average for this pipeline — four queries reported with IDs, the closest named method correctly identified and its claim quoted, SEC's venue correctly identified as a non-arXiv conference paper, and the empty seen/unseen query honestly reported as empty rather than spun as novelty, with the failed channels (WebSearch budget exhausted, S2 HTTP 429) disclosed. Its one substantive gap is that it never searched the memory-substrate/representation-comparison family, so it cites 2608.15008 in Related Work as 'substrate routing' without ever asking whether 'no substrate dominates' collides with 'abstraction is not the operative variable', and it missed 2603.02473 entirely. Novelty is scored on the verified position: the premise is published, the cue-level attribution is not.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That the raw-vs-distilled experience-memory disagreement is not about abstraction level at all but about two nameable content cues — source-scene object-to-receptacle bindings and failed-action-to-repair pairs — which can be annotated deterministically from ALFWorld logs and transplanted into and out of any representation at matched injected tokens, with the binding cue predicted to help only when the evaluation scene overlaps the memory pool's scenes and to actively harm otherwise.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The strongest threat I verified is arXiv:2604.14004, 'Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents' (2026-04-15, s2 verified), which already reports the proposal's headline interaction as an empirical design principle: 'abstraction dictates transferability; high-level insights generalize well, whereas low-level traces often induce negative transfer due to excessive specificity.' That is P1 (raw wins where the source context recurs, abstraction wins where it does not) plus the sign of P3 (over-specific detail causes negative transfer), already published, in coding agents across domains rather than in ALFWorld across room instances. It does not match tokens, does not name the cue classes inside the items, and does not transplant cues, so it does not scoop the identification design — but it removes most of the surprise from the proposal's two most prominent predictions, and the proposal neither cites nor found it. Second, arXiv:2506.06698 (CER, ACL, verified, 47 citations) already partitions accumulated experience into 'environment dynamics' and 'skills' — very nearly the binding-vs-procedure split the proposal presents as new — and arXiv:2604.05533 (Echo, verified) decomposes prior interactions into five knowledge dimensions for transfer to unseen tasks. The genuinely unclaimed part is narrow: the deterministic cue annotation, the plus/minus transplant at a matched token band, and the seen/unseen scene split as the moderator. SkillEvolBench (arXiv:2605.24117, verified on both s2 and hf) remains the proposal's correct anchor and does leave the cues unnamed, as claimed.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline claim — P5, 'after conditioning on the two cue indicators the residual representation effect is within MDE of zero' — is neither causally identified nor adequately powered, and it is the only prediction that would actually establish 'abstraction is not the variable.' (a) Identification: for the six base representations the cue indicators are caused by the representation, so conditioning on them to read off a 'residual representation main effect' is a controlled-direct-effect estimand that requires no unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding. Representations differ in register, imperative-vs-narrative form, step granularity, item count at fixed budget, and ordering — all plausible mediator-outcome confounders. The transplants do randomize cues within a representation, which is the right instrument, but the transplant arms only cover R1/R3/R5, while P5's falsification condition is stated over skill and graph (R4/R6), where no randomization exists at all. (b) Collinearity: by the stated annotation rule, essentially every raw trajectory contains a scene binding and essentially no insight does, so within the base cells the cue indicator is close to a deterministic function of representation and the model cannot separate them; the manual audit addresses annotator recall but not this near-collinearity. (c) Power: MDE is pre-registered at about 5 points net at n=400, but every prediction that matters is evaluated within a split at n=200, where MDE is roughly 7 points, and P2/P3/P4 are stated as fractions ('at least 70 percent', 'more than half') of raw's seen-scene advantage — an advantage this program's own starting position puts at +0.6 points on the 27B and +7.7 for SEC on the 120B. If raw's seen advantage is 6 points, 70 percent of it is 4 points, well inside noise at n=200 with 3 seeds. The confirmatory design is therefore built to test ratios of a quantity that may itself sit at the detection threshold, and a null P5 will be indistinguishable from an underpowered P5.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Three fixes, in order of importance. (1) Stop estimating 'abstraction per se' as a residual after conditioning on a post-treatment mediator. Extend the transplant grid to all six representations so every cue level is randomized within every representation; then the abstraction effect is the representation main effect in a fully crossed randomized design and needs no mediation assumption. Report it as a pre-registered equivalence test against a stated margin, not as a failure to reject. (2) Fix the power arithmetic before the confirmatory run: pilot raw's seen-scene advantage first, and if it is under about 10 points, either raise n per split (the local pool has 1,465 tasks, so 400 per split is achievable) or restate P2/P3/P4 as absolute point differences with pre-registered margins instead of percentages of a small effect. (3) Add the oracle-binding positive control described under missing_baseline, which is what makes P3 a mechanism result rather than a token-cost result. Two smaller repairs: pre-register the truncation rule for P6 (truncating raw from the front versus the back decides P6's outcome, since repair pairs sit late), and pre-register the room-level split before looking at outcomes, since the stated fallback to room-type splitting would gut the binding contrast and must not be chosen after seeing results.
reviews.missing_baseline: A correct-bindings-for-the-evaluation-scene arm on the unseen split: an oracle 60-token binding table describing the true object-receptacle layout of the room the agent is actually in, injected in the same slot and token band as the foreign table. Without it, P3's 'foreign bindings are harmful' is confounded with 'any binding table is useless or distracting once the scene is unfamiliar.' The relevance-matched decoy controls token load but not binding format — it does not show that a correctly-bound table in the same format would have helped. With the oracle arm, foreign-below-decoy-below-oracle is decisive evidence that the harm is wrong content adopted as fact, which is exactly what the first-move mediation analysis is supposed to demonstrate. A second omission a reviewer will raise: no retrieval-matched control isolating how much of the seen-scene advantage is retrieval selecting a near-duplicate task instance rather than the binding cue itself; retrieval overlap between the seen split and the pool should be measured and reported as a covariate.

reviews.one_line_contribution: It claims the raw-vs-distilled memory dispute is not about abstraction level but about two nameable content cues, scene bindings (object-to-receptacle facts, valuable only when the deployment scene recurs and harmful otherwise) and failure-to-repair pairs (scene-invariant), and it tests this by transplanting each cue into and out of six representations at matched injected-token budgets on ALFWorld seen/unseen room splits.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three, all verified via s2cli. (1) SkillEvolBench, arXiv:2605.24117 (verified; 2026-05-22) is the paper the proposal is answering, and it is also the main novelty problem: its own abstract already attributes raw-trajectory superiority to 'discarded contextual cues'. The proposed contribution is therefore to name and localize an explanation that is already in print, not to propose a new one; a reviewer will ask what is left if the answer turns out to be exactly what SkillEvolBench already said. (2) Demystifying Agent Skills, arXiv:2608.14036 (verified; 2026-08-14) is the closest methodological threat: it is already a controlled contrastive study with paired trajectory analysis that attributes skill gains to procedural anchoring rather than knowledge injection, i.e. a mechanism-attribution study of the same dispute. It does not do the seen/unseen split, the token matching or the cue transplant, so it does not scoop the design, but it does occupy the 'we explain why skills work' slot and its procedural-anchoring account competes directly with the failure-to-repair arm (a repair pair may help simply as an anchor, regardless of its content). (3) Contextual Experience Replay, arXiv:2506.06698 (verified; ACL 2025, 47 citations) already partitions accumulated experience into environment-specific dynamics and transferable skills, with ablations on each part. That is essentially the proposal's bindings-vs-repairs dichotomy, one benchmark family over (WebArena rather than ALFWorld), which materially reduces the novelty of the taxonomy itself; what survives is the token-matched transplant and the seen/unseen asymmetry, not the idea that memory contains an environment-specific component and a transferable one. Also verified and relevant: Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory arXiv:2508.15305 (EMNLP 2025) grounds environment-level information for ALFWorld planning.
reviews.strongest_objection: The binding construct may not exist in ALFWorld the way the proposal needs it to. ALFWorld/ALFRED resamples object placements across episodes: the receptacle inventory and the room layout are fixed per room instance, but which receptacle holds the target object is randomized per task instance. If so, a 'scene binding' harvested from a training trajectory in room R is not valid for a different task instance in room R, and raw's seen-scene advantage cannot be mediated by bindings at all. What would survive is a receptacle-type prior ('mugs are in cabinets and on countertops'), which is exactly the kind of cue that transfers to unseen rooms as well, collapsing the predicted split-by-cue interaction into noise for reasons of environment design rather than of hypothesis. The proposal's Risk section worries about whether the unseen side has enough tasks, but never about whether within-room bindings are stable across task instances, and no experiment validates the binding annotation against the next episode's ground truth. A second, independent hit on the same arm: the P5 headline ('after conditioning on the two cue indicators the residual effect of representation is within noise') is a regression adjustment for a post-treatment mediator measured by a heuristic annotator that the proposal itself expects to miss paraphrased bindings inside abstract representations. Mediator measurement error causes under-adjustment, which manufactures exactly the residual representation effect that P5 is set up to reject, so a null on P5 and a positive on P5 are both explainable by annotation quality; the 200-item manual audit calibrates the annotator but does not correct the estimate.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (a) Establish the binding construct before the confirmatory run: measure, on the local ALFWorld tasks, how often the object-to-receptacle pair recorded in a training trajectory still holds in a different task instance of the same room, and report that persistence rate. If it is low, redefine the cue as a receptacle-type prior and rewrite P2/P3, or move the seen/unseen contrast to an environment where scene state genuinely persists. (b) Add a cue-only representation (binding table alone, repair-pair list alone, both together) at the same 1,200-token budget; this is the direct test of 'the cues are the whole story' and it makes P5 an experimental comparison instead of a mediator regression. (c) Pre-register a multiplicity correction over the ~21 cells and six predictions, not just a per-comparison p<0.01. (d) Estimate the residual representation effect with the transplants as instruments or as a randomized within-item manipulation rather than by conditioning on an error-prone indicator, and report the annotator's measured sensitivity per representation so the adjustment can be corrected for attenuation. (e) Extend the transplant arms to R4/R6, since P5's falsification clause names skill and graph but only R1/R3/R5 get the machinery that could diagnose a residual there. (f) Add a step-count or object-location-search metric alongside binary success; binding value should show up in exploration cost long before it moves success, and at n=400 with a 5pp MDE the success-only design may be underpowered for the mediation claim in P3.
reviews.missing_baseline: A cue-only memory: the 60-token binding table and the mined failure-to-repair pairs injected on their own, with no carrier representation, at the same matched budget (and their union). The proposal appends cues to raw, insight and SEC-style records but never runs the cues by themselves, so it can show that adding or removing a cue moves success while still being unable to show that the cues are sufficient, which is what 'abstraction is not the variable' asserts. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also name: foreign/shuffled bindings on the seen split (the corruption control exists only on unseen), and an oracle binding table taken from the evaluation episode's own ground truth as an upper bound on what the binding channel can be worth.

(--recent) and 'ablating specific content components of retrieved memory items... mediation analysis' (--recent) returned nothing on point (2607.25853 HiSkill, 2607.10608 Compliance Trap, 2607.17621). ID verification: I verified arXiv:2605.24117, 2608.14036, 2603.25158, 2606.11680 (title is 'Organize then Retrieve: Hierarchical Memory Navigation for Efficient Agents', the proposal's 'HORM'), 2606.05684, 2512.07287, 2602.04288, 2605.06716, 2608.15008, 2412.15266, 2506.06698 and 2508.15305; every arXiv ID the novelty argument leans on resolved, and SEC's lack of an arXiv id is real, not a fabrication. On the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above average for this pipeline -- four queries, IDs attached, and it is honest that WebSearch was not run and that direct S2 calls 429'd. But it has one disqualifying inference. It ran a single query on the binding mechanism, got back only video and vision papers, and concluded 'the seen-versus-unseen binding mechanism appears unstudied'. That is an empty search treated as evidence of novelty, and the emptiness was an artifact of the query wording -- my rephrasing of the same idea surfaced Contextual Experience Replay (arXiv:2506.06698), whose environment-dynamics-versus-skills decomposition is the nearest thing to the proposal's two cue classes, plus Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory (arXiv:2508.15305) on grounding environment information for ALFWorld planning. Neither appears in the check or in Related Work. The check also never searched the failure-to-repair cue on its own, which is the arm with the most 2026 neighbours.
